items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: they tried him -- Dela Nova or something like that, an odd name.

ctx.x: Raymond Scott Quintet! Yeah, the drummer was named Johnny Williams, and he was supposed to be top. So they sent to New York to get him to do this, you know,but the trick in it, you know, you had to teach Mickey to play, you know, and there was a great drummer ... well,

Johnny couldn't do it because he couldn't teach Mickey, you know, and he had to play this whole thing. There was a great drummer on the staff over at Fox -- Twentieth Century Fox -- because that was when they had staff musicians, you know, and at this point I was not a staff musician, you know, I was just a freelance musician, and well, they tried him -- Dela Nova or something like that, an odd name.

But Georgie Stall used to come -- where I was playing; he had heard me, you know, Georgie Stall was kind of a jazz buff, and he made all of the rounds. And so he called me and told me I should come out and see if I couldn't get the gig, and so I went out to MGM the next day, and he met me at the gate, and they asked me -- I have to be honest -- I was really cocky at this point, you know, I was real cocky, because you know, I thought that I could just play anything, and I met with Georgie Stall and Alex Hyatt, his…
